I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is still the most dependable way for me to use the full year, spread risk, and keep grain output steady. At the start of this season, my wheat is already in the field from last autumn, so my main job now is to manage it carefully through jointing, heading, and grain filling, then harvest on time and follow immediately with summer maize. I would use improved seed rather than old saved seed because I want stable yield and better resistance, but I would not chase flashy high-input management. I would put most of my money into fertilizer at practical rates, timely irrigation, weed and disease control when needed, and getting the sowing and harvest windows right. For wheat, I would irrigate a few key times and keep the stand even; for maize, I would sow right after wheat harvest, keep population uniform, use no-tillage if possible to save time and moisture, and control weeds and insects early. My goal is steady output, manageable cost, and low risk rather than gambling on a more specialized crop.
